text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam's first-ever education law has been held over for the next session of the National Assembly due later this year.
-- Government Office Minister Lai Van Cu has warned of uneven development between Vietnam's central and local industrial sectors despite overall high growth rates.
-- Vietnam has applied to take part in three sub-groups of the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-orperation (APEC) Forum.
-- Twenty-two people including Vietnamese police officers will appear in court in Hanoi today at the start of a 10-day drugs trial.
-- The Ministry of Planning and Investment has expressed concern over a recent slight drop in foreign direct investment against the same period last year.
-- Tax exemptions will be applied to machinery and equipment imported for some 19 projects funded by French development aid, according to the Ministry of Finance.
